Three accent edges cross between them, B–D, C–D and C–E, so the cut size is 3.0." width="100%"} The number of edges with one end in `S` and the other in `T` (or their total weight on a weighted graph). `T` defaults to every node not in `S`, so the cut size measures how strongly a group is tied to the rest of the network: small cuts separate natural communities, which is what partitioning and community detection look for. On a directed graph, edges in both directions count. The other cut measures (`conductance()`, `normalized_cut_size()`, `edge_expansion()`, `mixing_expansion()`) build on it. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [S]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list[Union[int, str]]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : One set of nodes, as integer IDs or string labels. [T]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list[Union[int, str]] | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : The other set. If `None` (default), all nodes not in `S`. [weighted]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Whether to sum edge weights instead of counting edges. If `None` (default), follows the graph. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The cut size. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `S=` is empty or a node does not exist. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Two triangles joined by one edge have a cut of size 1 between them: ::: {#aeb0f191 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_nodes(["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]) .add_edges([("A", "B"), ("B", "C"), ("C", "A"), ("C", "D"), ("D", "E"), ("E", "F"), ("F", "D")]) ) graph.cut_size(["A", "B", "C"]), graph.cut_size(["A", "B"]) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (1.0, 2.0) ``` ::: :::
